processes.name: React single-page web app
processes.description: Publicly loadable React single-page web application that calls the Orders API.
processes.source_excerpt: Anyone can load our React single-page web app without signing in

processes.name: CloudFront
processes.description: Serves the React single-page web app to the public internet.
processes.source_excerpt: CloudFront serves it to the public internet over HTTPS with TLS 1.3

processes.name: Orders API
processes.description: Internal API that processes orders, accesses the database, payment service, and audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: The web app calls an internal Orders API in our AWS VPC over HTTPS

processes.name: AWS WAF
processes.source_excerpt: AWS WAF on CloudFront limits each client to 2,000 requests per five minutes

processes.name: Nightly batch job
processes.description: Batch job that reads one day of orders and writes summaries to S3.
processes.source_excerpt: A nightly batch job in the VPC reads at most one day of orders

processes.name: Athena
processes.description: Service through which the analytics team queries the S3 bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: query that bucket through Athena, which reads it over TLS

processes.name: Admin console
processes.description: Console used by support administrators to refund orders, edit delivery addresses, and look up order history.
processes.source_excerpt: use an admin console on the Orders API

data_stores.name: Postgres database
data_stores.description: Database holding customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It holds customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history, is encrypted at rest with AWS KMS

data_stores.name: S3 bucket
data_stores.description: KMS-encrypted bucket that stores nightly batch summaries.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes summaries over HTTPS, with its own IAM role, to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket

data_stores.name: CloudWatch Logs audit log
data_stores.description: Audit log storing Orders API administrative actions that administrators cannot change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: CloudWatch Logs audit log that administrators cannot change

data_stores.name: Database snapshot
data_stores.description: Snapshots of the Postgres database that the platform team can copy or restore.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Only the platform team can copy or restore the database snapshots

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Customer sign-in using a password and MFA.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers sign in to our Auth0 identity provider over HTTPS with TLS 1.3, using a password and MFA

data_flows.name: load web app
data_flows.description: Customer loads the public React single-page web app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Anyone can load our React single-page web app without signing in; CloudFront serves it to the public internet over HTTPS with TLS 1.3

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: Web app calls the Orders API with an Auth0 OAuth2 bearer token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web app calls an internal Orders API in our AWS VPC over HTTPS. Every call carries an Auth0 OAuth2 bearer token

data_flows.name: access orders
data_flows.description: Orders API reads and writes customer and order data in the Postgres database.

data_flows.data_description: Customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history

data_flows.description: Orders API sends payment authorisation to Stripe using a secret API key.

data_flows.data_description: Payment authorisation and secret API key

data_flows.data_description: At most one day of orders

data_flows.name: write summaries
data_flows.description: Nightly batch job writes summaries to the S3 bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes summaries over HTTPS, with its own IAM role, to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket

data_flows.name: query summaries
